Open source · Apple Silicon · One Mac, your whole network

LAW: a private AI team
on a single Mac

LAW turns a 64 GB Apple Silicon Mac into an AI workstation for everyone on your network. A team of agents plans, builds and tests software end to end, answers and researches with sources, writes proposals and reports, operates apps on your Mac, and makes images, video, speech and music, all on open models that run on the Mac itself. Before you see any answer, a model of a different family has checked it.

Get started See it working Read the documentation View on GitHub

Source: github.com/mthaqifisa/local-ai-workstation · free and open source

Why LAW

Cloud AI is fast to start and hard to trust with your work: your data leaves the building, the bill grows with use, and the model that writes an answer is usually the only one that checks it. LAW is built the other way round.

Private by design

Models run on the Mac. Documents, code and conversations stay on your network. Secrets live in one file outside the repository, and git hooks block personal data from ever being committed.

Never grades its own work

Every answer goes through draft, independent review and revision. The reviewer is a different model family, so one model's blind spots are not approved by the same model. Numbers are computed in code, never guessed.

Free to run

Open models and open-source tools only: no licence fees, no subscriptions, no per-token bill. Every model and tool is pinned to an exact version, so an install today matches an install next year.

What it does

Software, end to end

Describe a product on Telegram. Agents write a proposal and a plan you approve, build it ticket by ticket, test the running product as a black box every round, fix what QA finds and hand over a document with real screenshots. After every ticket LAW runs the project's own build and tests itself: the agent's word is never taken for it.

A coding agent on call

/code or law code works in any project folder: new features, fixes and refactors, kept honest by the project's build, lint and tests. /bugfix reports a bug; the coder fixes it and QA retests the product.

Answers and research with sources

Chat in Telegram, Open WebUI or the terminal, with private web search, your documents and knowledge bases, and a calculator the model must use for any figure. Replies show the model's live reasoning.

Proposals, reports and books

/proposal researches and writes a consultant-grade proposal as a PDF. /rnd writes reports, research papers and books chapter by chapter: every fact quoted from a saved source, code samples that compile, and an independent editor.

An agent that uses your Mac

The operator opens apps, plays music, changes the volume and settings, runs Shortcuts and takes screenshots to check its own work: "play calm jazz on Spotify at 25% volume" just happens.

Images, video, speech and music

Generate and edit images, animate a still, make a short film with planned shots, a score and cuts, compose full songs with lyrics, speak text in natural voices and transcribe recordings.

A team of specialists

Architect, analyst, designer, researcher, writer, translator, coder, reviewer and QA: each role has its own instructions, tools and model, and you can call any of them directly with /agent.

Your Mac as an AI server

OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible APIs for VS Code, Claude Code, scripts and apps on every device on your network, and it keeps working without internet once the models are downloaded.

You stay in charge

Plans and key changes wait for your Go on Telegram. When an agent is stuck, a lead developer drafts a note and you approve, edit or drop it. /note steers a running agent at its next step; the Console shows every agent live.

How it works

  1. You askFrom Telegram, the terminal, a browser or the API.
  2. LAW schedulesOne durable queue; the scheduler loads the model that fits in memory.
  3. An agent worksResearch, writing, code or media, saved as it goes, so nothing is lost.
  4. Checks runThe project's own build and tests, then a reviewer of another model family.
  5. You decidePlans, notes and final results come to you for a Go.

A single Mac holds one large model at a time, so the scheduler swaps 30–45 GB models in and out as jobs need them: a reasoning model with speculative decoding for planning, writing and code, a fast coder, a fast assistant and operator, an independent judge, a document editor, and media models for images, video, speech and music. The full picture, with every component and port, is in Architecture.

Get started

git clone -b v6-simplified-mlx https://github.com/mthaqifisa/local-ai-workstation.git ~/SourceCode/OpenSourceLocalAI/v6
cd ~/SourceCode/OpenSourceLocalAI/v6
./install.sh        # safe to run again: it only changes what is out of date
law doctor          # checks every service and prints the addresses on your network

You need an Apple Silicon Mac with 64 GB of memory, Homebrew and Python, and room for the models: the first install downloads about 200 GB, and a Mac with every optional model holds about 300 GB. The Quick start covers the first ten minutes, the Runbook covers updates and troubleshooting, and Architecture explains every component. The rest of this page is the full documentation.

Overview

A private, free, open-source AI server for an Apple Silicon Mac (built and tested on an M5 Pro, 64 GB). It runs strong open models locally for chat, judgement, coding, documents, image generation and editing, speech and music, and serves them to every device on your network.

Quality comes first: answers go through a draft → independent review → revise loop where the reviewer is a different model family from the writer, so the system never grades its own work.

What you get

Use it from How
Telegram (main channel) Message your bot: text, voice notes, photos; /help lists every command (/image, /video, /music, /code, /project, /rnd, /bugfix, /qa, /note, …). Replies show live thinking
Terminal law ask "…", law code "…", law image "…", law tts "…", law stt file.wav, law music "…", law jobs, law api <Class>, law qa <project>, law bugfix <project> [bug], law board show <project>, law send <file>
Browser (on the Mac; from other devices use the Mac’s address, printed by law doctor) Open WebUI chat http://127.0.0.1:3000 · LAW Console http://127.0.0.1:8100 (live stats, agents, project boards, services, jobs, personas, settings) · dashboard http://127.0.0.1:3010 · Docker (Portainer, user admin, password PORTAINER_ADMIN_PASSWORD in ~/LAW/state/.env) http://127.0.0.1:9000
Any OpenAI/Anthropic client http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1

Agents do the work, end to end. Describe a product and a team of agents writes the proposal and a plan you approve on Telegram, builds it ticket by ticket, tests the running product, fixes what QA finds and hands it over (/project, or /code for code only). The same team writes consultant-grade proposals (/proposal), reports, research papers and books (/rnd), operates apps on your Mac (/agent operator), and makes images, video, songs and short films. Every project’s progress shows live on the Console’s board.

Every request goes through one durable job queue with a scheduler that knows how much memory each model needs. Big models are swapped in and out as needed, so you can use 30–45 GB models one at a time on 64 GB.

Architecture

How a request flows

Coding tasks follow the same idea at project scale: translate (the request becomes a precise brief: goal, requirements, acceptance criteria, assumptions) → work (coder agent) → review → fix if the review fails. For projects, every review round has two independent checks, both on Gemma (another model family than the Qwen coder):

  1. Black-box QA tests the product, never the code. In a fresh session it starts the app as the README says, runs its regression pack (<project>/qa/), then checks every requirement and acceptance criterion through the app itself (headless browser, HTTP API, commands) and the edges a user hits. A guard stops it reading source files. Bugs go to <project>/.law/BUGS.md with steps, expected and actual result, evidence and a severity (blocker, major, minor); only QA can close a bug, after retesting it.
  2. Code review reads the code against the spec and runs the project’s checks.

A round passes only when no blocker or major bug is open and the code review passes (ADR-0018).

Every project keeps its working memory in <project>/.law/ (like .claude/ for Claude Code): PROMPT.md (the brief), REQUESTS.md (every request and every note you sent the agent), RESEARCH.md, PLAN.md (steps with checkboxes and gates), PROGRESS.md (done, gate output, next step), BUGS.md (QA’s and your bug reports) and ENVIRONMENT.md / env.sh (the tools the stack needs). .law/.gitignore is an allow-list: only these files are ever committed, so a scratch file or a key an agent drops there cannot reach git. The agent keeps them current and continues from them, so a session that dies halfway picks up where it stopped; a restarted job resumes its own agent session (.law/session.json, git-ignored). With no folder given, the translator names the project folder (an existing one only when you name that project) and LAW creates it directly under ~/SourceCode/.

How quality is enforced

  • Independent judge: a different model family scores every answer against a rubric; weak drafts are revised.
  • No mental arithmetic: roles that handle numbers must use the run_python calculator; the judge recomputes figures.
  • Bounded reasoning: each role has a reasoning effort, so the model can’t think itself out of an answer.
  • Agent work is reviewed: code and documents get a read-and-run review by the judge and a fix pass; projects also get black-box QA of the running product every round (above).
  • Reviews are real: the judge keeps most of its context for reading (output capped at 6K tokens), and a review that ends without findings runs again instead of being turned into a score.
  • Stuck agents are caught: a writing agent that saves nothing for 25 minutes is stopped and resumed in the same session with a nudge (coders: build and fix the first error; writers: save the next section), up to 3 times. A long single generation gets up to 45 minutes; an agent busy reading without saving does not.
  • Nothing is lost when a step dies: agents keep a to-do list and progress in .law/, write big files section by section, and LAW records a step in .law/PROGRESS.md itself when the agent did not. Instructions are looked up when each step runs, so retries and long projects always use the current rules.
  • Agents are kept on track: an agent that keeps looking up APIs without writing code (law api research budget), reads library internals (jars, node_modules, a library’s source on GitHub), or reads LAW’s own source or state (secrets) is stopped and pointed to the supported way. Coders print the exact data when a test fails on data, and search an unfamiliar error’s text before guessing.
  • You can steer a running agent: /note <project> <text> reaches it at its next action. When an agent stays stuck, a lead developer (the agent’s own model) drafts a note and Tony sends it to you with Approve / Edit / Drop; only what you approve reaches the agent, and a draft waits for your answer however long it takes.
  • LAW does the bookkeeping: after each ticket LAW runs the project’s gate itself, then commits, ticks the ticket and records progress; the agent’s word is never taken for it. A gate step that never ran (an unknown command) fails.
  • Documents are written for their readers (reports, papers and books from /rnd): facts come from saved, quoted sources, code samples compile and pass their tests, every term is explained where the reader first meets it, and a checker fails long sentences and unreadable diagrams. An editor of another model family checks every section against its sources and its intended readers (docs/adr/0031-book-reader-panel-and-readability-gate.md).
  • Measured claims: agents that benchmark LAW itself run with no other request on the model and check ~/LAW/logs/omlx.log; documents are checked as a reader sees them (text extraction and page images).
  • Safe updates: law install never restarts the worker mid-step; it restarts between steps.
  • House standard in every role: answer first, sourced claims, no invented facts, units or currencies.
  • Measured: law eval runs a verified golden set through the real product; scripts/test_report.py writes docs/TEST-REPORT.md.

Security posture

Chosen by the owner for a home network: user-facing services are open to the LAN without login, and agents act with the user’s permissions (open apps, run commands). Telegram, being internet-reachable, answers only allow-listed user IDs. Valkey and oMLX bind to loopback. Secrets live only in ~/LAW/state/.env (mode 600). Don’t run LAW on untrusted networks (hotel or office Wi-Fi). See docs/adr/0006-network-and-access.md.

This repo is public, so git hooks (.githooks/, set up by law install) and gitleaks rules (.gitleaks.toml) block commits and pushes that contain secrets or personal data: email addresses, home-folder paths, Mac hostnames or LAN addresses. Commits use the GitHub noreply address only. See docs/adr/0023-privacy-guards-public-repo.md.

Ports

Every port LAW opens, from settings/registry.yaml (ports:). “LAN” means 0.0.0.0 with no login (see above).

Port Service Binds to Used by
3000 Open WebUI (chat, RAG, voice) LAN Browsers on any device
3010 Homepage dashboard LAN Browsers; embedded in the Console’s Services tab
6379 Valkey (job queue) loopback LAW API and worker only
8000 Caddy, the LAN front door to the LLM API LAN OpenAI/Anthropic clients, VS Code, Claude Code, apps the agents build
8001 oMLX (LLM, VLM, embeddings, rerank) loopback Caddy, the worker and OpenCode
8100 LAW job API and LAW Console LAN law CLI, Telegram bot, Console, law on other machines
8110 Read-only Console loopback The only port that is safe to forward to the internet (ADR-0022)
8188 ComfyUI LAN Image/video workflows
8888 SearXNG LAN Web search for agents and chat
9000 Portainer (own admin login) LAN Docker management

The Telegram bot uses long polling, so it opens no inbound port. Projects the agents build publish their own ports while they run (Pantry, for example, uses 443, 8080 and 5432); those come from each project’s compose.yaml, not from LAW. To change a port, edit settings/registry.yaml and run law install.

Install

On a new or freshly formatted Mac with Homebrew and Python installed:

git clone -b v6-simplified-mlx https://github.com/mthaqifisa/local-ai-workstation.git ~/SourceCode/OpenSourceLocalAI/v6
cd ~/SourceCode/OpenSourceLocalAI/v6
./install.sh            # safe to run again any time
law doctor              # health check + the addresses to use from your other devices

The first run downloads about 200 GB of models. Later runs change only what differs from settings/. The repo can live anywhere under any folder name. If you move or rename it after installing, run ./install.sh once from the new location: it points the law command, the services and your shell profile at the new place.

Set up Telegram

LAW answers through a Telegram bot that you own. It only replies to the Telegram accounts you allow.

The easy way: ./install.sh asks you. Whenever Telegram isn’t set up and you run ./install.sh in a Terminal, it:

  1. Asks for the bot token (typing is hidden). Get it from @BotFather in Telegram: /newbot for a new bot, or /mybots → your bot (e.g. “Tony”) → API Token.
  2. Checks the token with Telegram and shows the bot’s name, e.g. Connected to @TonyBot.
  3. Asks you to send the bot any message from your phone or Mac, then press Enter. It lists who just messaged the bot (e.g. 1. Alex (@alex) [id 512345678]); pick yourself (and anyone else to allow).
  4. Saves both to ~/LAW/state/.env (readable only by you, never in the repo) and starts the bot.
  5. Asks for your report email: where LAW sends finished documents such as /proposal PDFs, through this Mac’s Mail app (no mail password is stored). Change it any time in the LAW Console → Settings.

Press Enter at the first prompt to skip; it will ask again on the next run. Before you start, make sure no other program is running the same bot (an old setup or another server): a bot can only be connected to one program at a time.

Check it with law doctor (should show Telegram: configured, 1 allowed id(s)), then send the bot hello.

Manual alternative (scripts, or changing it later):

law secrets set LAW_TELEGRAM_TOKEN 123456789:AAH...
law secrets set LAW_TELEGRAM_USER_IDS 512345678            # several: 512345678,698765432
law install

What you can send

Message What happens
Any text Answered on the fast model, remembering the conversation (“continue”, “yes” carry on); long answers go through the quality loop (draft → independent review → revise). Work that needs files, commands or documents (a report, a PDF, building or fixing software, research) is handed to the right agent, which reports back in the same chat
Voice note Transcribed, then answered
Photo (optionally with a caption) Described or answered about, using the vision model
/project init Start a full project (SDLC): Tony sends a template (name, repo, repo URL, stack, thinking level, proposal depth brief/full, summary, details). Send it back filled in, and Tony researches and emails a proposal (PDF, also posted in Telegram), asks Go / No go, sets up the tools the stack needs, builds in milestones (a ticket board in .law/PLAN.md; a fresh agent session per ticket, and after each one LAW itself runs the project’s whole gate, .law/check.sh, and hands any failure to the next session), tests and fixes until an independent review passes, writes a system handover document with real screenshots (emailed), then asks you to verify. Needs changes brings an enhanced proposal (v2, v3, …) and the loop repeats until All good. Decide with the buttons or /go, /nogo, /changes, /allgood; /projects shows where each one is; /email <project> resends its latest document
/code init Code only: the same template without the proposal depth. Tony posts a short plan in the chat (what it will build, stack and versions, milestones, tests, assumptions) and asks Go / No go (No go with notes revises the plan). On Go: tools, milestones, tests, independent review, then your verification with how to run it. No research, PDFs or email; add documents later with /proposal <folder>
/code <task> The coding agent builds a new project in its own folder under ~/SourceCode/ (named after the project you describe)
/code <folder> <task> Works in that project, e.g. /code ~/SourceCode/my-app add a login page; a new folder name (e.g. ~/SourceCode/new-app) is created
/proposal [<folder>] <request> A consultant-grade proposal: web research with sources, then a full document (executive summary, market, solution, technical design, architecture, user and system flows, wireframes, delivery plan, cost, risks), independently reviewed, rendered to PDF and emailed to you. Give a project folder to present it as the working prototype
/image <prompt> Generates an image and sends it back
/music <request> A full song: theme, genre/vibe and length (e.g. 2 min). Tony writes the lyrics, or add a lyrics: line with your own; say instrumental for no vocals
/film <request> A short film (up to 2 min): shots planned from your theme or a script: section, rendered with fast Wan 2.2, scored and cut together. Say no music to skip the score
/agent <role> <task> Runs a role, e.g. /agent architect design a payments API or /agent operator play jazz on Spotify
/jobs [project or keyword] What’s running and its health: 🟢 working, 🔵 thinking, 🟠 stalled/stuck, 🔴 failed. With a keyword: the step, last action, to-do progress and model activity, with Retry / Skip / Restart / Cancel buttons
/retry <job> Run a failed job again from the step that failed (earlier work is kept). Every failed job also asks you Retry / Skip with buttons
/note <project> <text> Tells the agent working on a project something while it works; it gets the note at its next action (also on the project’s board)
/bugfix <project> <what goes wrong> Reports a bug (in .law/BUGS.md and on the board). While the project builds, the working agent fixes it after its current step and QA retests it; otherwise the coder fixes it and QA retests the product, up to 3 rounds, and you get the result. /bugfix <project> alone fixes every open bug
/qa <project> QA tests the running product now (black box, including the regression pack) and lists open bugs by severity. QA never runs on a schedule: only when you ask or inside a build you started. A new blocker is sent to you at once with its steps and screenshot
/new · /hardreset Start a new conversation (Tony forgets the chat) · wipe all jobs, history and caches (asks first; keeps models, settings and projects)

A status message updates live while the job runs. Messages from accounts that aren’t on your list are ignored.

Change or remove later: run law secrets set … again, then law install. To move to a new Mac, law secrets export ~/Desktop/law-secrets.env saves the token and IDs to a file you keep privately; on the new Mac run ./install.sh --secrets ~/Desktop/law-secrets.env.

Troubleshooting: no reply → law services logs telegram. “Conflict: terminated by other getUpdates request” means another program is still using the same bot (step 3).

Use this Mac as an offline AI server for other machines

Everything LAW needs runs on this Mac, so another laptop on the same Wi-Fi can use its AI to write code with no internet at all (for example a home router that isn’t connected to the internet). Verified on 2026-10-20 by running OpenCode in a sandbox with internet blocked: it wrote and tested code using only this Mac’s model.

Before you go offline (once, on the other machine, with internet)

  1. Install OpenCode (the coding agent): brew install opencode (macOS/Linux) or npm install -g opencode-ai (any OS).
  2. Install the tools your projects need (Python, Node, JDK, pytest, npm install in each project, …). Offline, the AI can still write code, but nothing can be downloaded, so dependencies must already be there.
  3. Optional: VS Code with the Continue extension (see below), also installed while online.

At home without internet

  1. Connect both machines to the same Wi-Fi.

  2. On this Mac, check the server is up and note its address:

    law doctor        # all "up"; the address is shown under "LAN access"

    The Mac’s name is <mac-name>.local (e.g. my-macbook.local); it works without internet (Bonjour). If the name doesn’t resolve, use the IP address from law doctor instead.

  3. On the other machine, run the one-line setup this Mac serves (writes the OpenCode config and settings into your shell profile; safe to run again):

    curl -fsSL http://<mac-name>.local:8100/client/install.sh | sh

  4. Open a new terminal on the other machine, go to your project and start the agent:

    cd ~/code/my-project
opencode

    It uses this Mac’s coding model (Qwen3.8-27B) and edits the files on the other machine.

  5. Check, if anything seems off:

    curl http://<mac-name>.local:8000/v1/models     # lists the models: the network path works

VS Code (Continue extension)

In Continue’s config (~/.continue/config.yaml):

models:
  - name: LAW Qwen3.8 (home server)
    provider: openai
    model: qwen3.8-27b-8bit
    apiBase: http://<mac-name>.local:8000/v1
    apiKey: local
    roles: [chat, edit, apply]

Claude Code (optional)

Claude Code can also use this Mac’s Anthropic-compatible endpoint. Install and start it once while online, then:

export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://<mac-name>.local:8000
export ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=local
export ANTHROPIC_MODEL=qwen3.8-27b-8bit
export ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL=qwen3.8-27b-8bit
export CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1
claude

OpenCode is the recommended client offline: it is open source and the setup above was tested with internet blocked.

Good to know

  • The Mac holds one large model at a time. While it runs a heavy job (an agent, an image or video), a request for a different large model gets a “cannot load … memory” error; retry when law jobs shows it finished, or use the model that’s already loaded.
  • law code / law agent jobs (and Telegram /code) run on this Mac’s files in ~/SourceCode. To work on the other machine’s files, use OpenCode/Continue there as above.
  • The law command also works from the other machine for non-coding jobs (images, music, questions): export LAW_SERVER=http://<mac-name>.local:8100 (set by the setup script) and install law with uv tool install --python 3.12 <path-to-v6> while online.
  • No login is needed on the LAN (owner’s choice); don’t run LAW on untrusted networks.

Software the agents build can use LAW

Apps the agents build may call LAW at runtime (the development rules tell them how; ADR-0018 and the dev spec):

  • LLM: http://<host>:8000/v1 (OpenAI-compatible) with LAW’s fast model; from a Docker container the Mac is host.docker.internal. HTTP 507 means another model holds LAW’s memory (e.g. an agent is working): busy, not an answer. The first call after idle loads the model (~10 s).
  • Web search: SearXNG on port 8888.
  • Message the owner: law send --message "…" on the Mac, or from a container POST http://host.docker.internal:8100/send with {"text": "…"} (Telegram, allow-listed chats only; no bot token in the project).

Where things live

Location What Survives a format?
v6/ (git) Code, settings/ (models, ports, roles), knowledge/, trained/, docs Yes, via git
~/LAW/ Models, caches, containers, generated media, logs, secrets (state/.env) No, and that’s fine
LAW Console → Agents Live health of every running job (working / thinking / stalled / stuck / failed), its step, last actions, to-do progress and the model’s activity, with Retry / Skip / Restart / Cancel —
<project>/.law/ A project’s brief, requests, research, plan, progress and bug list (commit it with the project) With the project
<project>/qa/ QA’s regression pack: black-box checks of the product, re-run every QA round (written by QA only) With the project
LAW Console → Projects A Jira-style board per project, built from what the agents record (stages and their logs, the coder’s PLAN.md tickets and commits, BUGS.md): proposal, QA, development, bug fixes, your approvals, with notes —
<project>/docs/proposal/ or ~/LAW/outputs/docs/ /proposal research, Markdown source, diagrams, wireframes, PDF With the project

Disk use is bounded: the LLM’s SSD prompt cache is capped by machine.llm_ssd_cache_gb in settings/registry.yaml (default 20 GB), agent build caches (Maven, npm, Gradle, pip, uv) go to ~/LAW/cache, and law reclaim removes retired models, stale downloads and old logs. History is kept for 14 days by default (retention: in the registry: finished jobs, agent conversations, logs, trash), pruned every 6 hours. The Console’s Storage tab shows every cache with its size and what clearing it costs, clears them with a button, and edits the retention and the prompt-cache limit.

Things you create in Open WebUI (model presets, prompts, tools, functions, knowledge-base definitions) are kept in the repo with law save, which writes settings/openwebui/, refuses to save if it finds anything that looks like a secret, and commits locally. law install on another Mac adds them back (law restore-state does it on demand). Valves, chats, users and uploaded documents are not exported.

No secrets are ever stored in the repo. To reset everything machine-local: law uninstall && rm -rf ~/LAW.

Docs

  • Quick start: first 10 minutes
  • Runbook: operate, update, troubleshoot
  • Architecture and decision records
  • Research: why these models and tools
  • Documentation page: all of the above on one page (open it in a browser)

Quick start

1. Check it’s healthy

law doctor

All rows should say up. On the Mac itself, the services are at:

Chat / Open WebUI : http://127.0.0.1:3000
LLM API           : http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1
Dashboard         : http://127.0.0.1:3010
LAW Console       : http://127.0.0.1:8100

From your other devices, use the Mac’s address instead of 127.0.0.1: the bottom of law doctor’s output prints it, or use the Mac’s network name, http://<mac-name>.local:3000.

Open the LAW Console at http://127.0.0.1:8100 (or the Mac’s address from another device): live CPU/memory/GPU/storage of the Mac, running jobs with a Cancel button, persona editing, and Telegram settings.

2. Ask something

law ask "Compare leasing vs buying a company car for a 10-person firm"
law ask --role architect "Design a document-approval workflow for a small bank"
law ask --quick "What is 17% of 2,340?"      # skips the review loop for quick questions

By default every answer is drafted, reviewed by an independent model, and revised if the review finds gaps. Progress lines (… stage 2/3: judge) show where it is.

Roles: assistant (default), architect, coder, reviewer, writer, analyst, designer, researcher, operator.

3. Create things

law image "A clean isometric illustration of a data centre, pastel colours"
law edit photo.jpg "Remove the background and make it pure white"
law tts "Good morning. Here is today's summary."
law stt meeting.m4a
law music "Calm lo-fi piano for focus" --duration 60
law video "A paper boat drifting down a rain-soaked street at dusk, cinematic" --seconds 5
law video --image boat.png "The boat slowly drifts forward as rain falls"

Video uses Wan 2.2 (14B) and takes several minutes per clip; it runs one at a time in the queue.

Files land in ~/LAW/outputs/{images,audio,video,docs}; the command prints the path.

4. Code with an agent

mkdir -p ~/SourceCode/expense-tracker
law code --dir ~/SourceCode/expense-tracker "Build a FastAPI expense tracker with SQLite, tests and a README"

5. Let an agent use your Mac

The operator role can open apps, play music, change the volume, run Shortcuts and take screenshots to check its work.

law agent operator "Play some calm jazz on Spotify and set the volume to 25%"

macOS asks once for permission (Accessibility, Automation, Screen Recording) the first time each app is controlled. Approve it in System Settings → Privacy & Security.

6. Telegram

  1. In Telegram, talk to @BotFather → /newbot → copy the token.

  2. Get your numeric user ID from @userinfobot.

  3. Put both in LAW and restart the bot:

    ./install.sh --secrets my-secrets.env   # file with LAW_TELEGRAM_TOKEN=... and LAW_TELEGRAM_USER_IDS=...

  4. Message your bot: plain text to ask, a voice note to talk, a photo with a caption. Tap the menu button next to the attachment icon (or send /help) for every command: /image, /edit (photo caption), /video, /animate (photo caption), /music (add lyrics: for your own words, and a duration like 90s), /say, /code, /agent, /search, /jobs, /cancel. While Tony works, its status message shows live thinking.

7. Build a project end to end

  1. Send /project init, fill in the template Tony returns (name, stack, what it must do) and send it back.
  2. Tony researches and emails a proposal PDF; press Go to build (or No go with what to change).
  3. The agents set up the tools, build milestone by milestone (one fresh session per ticket, each checked by LAW’s own run of .law/check.sh), then run review rounds: black-box QA tests the running product against your requirements and files bugs, the coder fixes them, QA retests. Follow it on the Console’s Projects board.
  4. While it builds: /note <project> <text> tells the agent something; /bugfix <project> <what goes wrong> reports a bug; /qa <project> re-tests the product whenever you want (QA never runs on a schedule).
  5. You get a handover document (with a “check on your phone” list) and verify: All good or Needs changes.

8. Use it from another computer

export LAW_SERVER=http://<mac-name>.local:8100
law ask "…"        # runs on the AI Mac

Any OpenAI-compatible app can use http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1 on the Mac (from another computer, the Mac’s address in place of 127.0.0.1) with any API key.

Runbook

Daily use

Task Command
Health + LAN addresses law doctor
Live stats, jobs (cancel), personas, settings LAW Console: http://127.0.0.1:8100
Approve a plan or build Console, Projects: the button in Waiting for approval (same as /go or /allgood)
Redo a project’s plan, proposal and tickets Tell Tony. Agents write the new version and tickets (the old ones leave the board) and it waits for your go
See the Console from the internet (read only) VS Code Ports panel: forward 8110, keep visibility Private. Never forward 8100: it has no login and can change everything (ADR-0022)
One-line status law status
Recent jobs law jobs
Talk to Tony Just type in Telegram: Tony remembers the recent conversation (/new starts over), answers short questions in seconds, and hands work that needs files, code, documents or apps to an agent that reports in the same chat (ADR-0017)
QA a project now /qa <project> in Telegram or law qa <project>: black-box test of the running product, open bugs listed by severity. Only on request: QA never runs on a schedule
Fix every open bug /bugfix <project> (no text) or law bugfix <project>: fix, then QA retest, up to 3 rounds
Report a bug in a project /bugfix <project> <what goes wrong, what you expected> in Telegram: logged in <project>/.law/BUGS.md and on the board; the agent fixes it, then QA retests the running product (ADR-0018)
Start completely fresh /hardreset in Telegram (asks first): stops all jobs, deletes job history, agent conversations, Tony’s chat memory and every LAW cache. Keeps models, settings, secrets, projects with their .law/, generated files, and the jobs of unfinished projects (Retry still continues them). Console: POST /reset
Send a file to yourself (what agents use) law send report.pdf (Telegram) · law send report.pdf --email --subject "Report" (Mail.app; --to for another address)
Message yourself from an app in a container POST http://host.docker.internal:8100/send with {"text": "..."} (Telegram, allow-listed chats; 503 if Telegram is not set up)
Real API of a library symbol (what coding agents use instead of guessing; ADR-0016) Java law api StompSession subscribe · Go law api net/http.Client Do · TS law api @angular/core:signal · Swift law api View navigationTitle · Monkey C law api WatchUi.View
Deploying while agents work law install prints “restarts on the new code between steps”
Disk filling up Console → Storage (sizes per cache)
Is an agent working, thinking or stuck? Console → Agents, or /jobs <project> in Telegram
A job failed or got stuck Retry (from the failed step, earlier work kept), Skip (carry on without that step) or Restart step (stuck); buttons in the Console and Telegram, or law retry <id>
Cancel a job law cancel <id> (cancelling a pipeline also stops its running stage and agent process)
Service log law services logs worker (also api, omlx, caddy, valkey, telegram, comfyui)
Restart a service law services restart worker
Models on disk law models list

All logs are in ~/LAW/logs/.

Change settings

Everything is declared in settings/ (git):

  • settings/registry.yaml: models, memory budget, ports, media tools, pinned versions
  • settings/roles.yaml: personas and their tools
  • compose.yaml: Open WebUI, SearXNG, Homepage, Portainer (ADR-0019)
  • Brewfile: system packages

Edit, commit, then run ./install.sh (or law install). It applies only the difference: registry changes restart the API, worker and Telegram bot; other services restart only when their own settings change. Preview first with law install --dry-run.

Swap or add a model

  1. Find an MLX build on Hugging Face and note its commit SHA (revision).
  2. Add or edit an entry under llm_models: with repo, revision, mem_gb, lane, roles.
  3. law install. The download is verified and marked complete; law reclaim later frees the old one.

Keep every heavy model’s mem_gb within machine.model_budget_gb (48 GB); the registry refuses anything larger.

Personas

Edit a role’s instructions, temperature, reasoning effort or tools in the Console (Personas tab) or in settings/roles.yaml. Saving in the Console validates the change, keeps the file’s comments and re-applies the agents. A role’s temperature applies only to a model without sampling in settings/registry.yaml; the three LLMs run at their model cards’ sampling (ADR-0020). A new model gets its card’s values there.

Project boards

The Console’s Projects tab shows one board per project (pick it in the dropdown), with the columns To do, In progress, Waiting for approval, Completed and Failed / cancelled. The board is built from what LAW already records, so it never needs updating by hand:

  • proposal writing, its review (QA) and delivery; the environment stage; each QA review round and the fix round for the bugs it reported; the handover document: from the project’s pipeline stages and their logs;
  • go / no go and verification gates: Waiting for approval until the owner decides in Telegram;
  • development tickets: .law/PLAN.md (- [ ] P-6 ... under ### M2 ...), with their commits (P-6: ...), .law/PROGRESS.md entries and the agent’s actions while the ticket was open.

Click a ticket for its details, steps, notes and logs. Notes are stored in ~/LAW/state/boards/<project>.json. A note names its ticket, or is pinned to the ticket in progress when it was written (Telegram /note works this way):

law board show pantry
law board note pantry "P-17: container apps use POST /send" --ticket P-17 --author "Claude (build session)"
law board note pantry "use the PEM files" --to-agent      # the ticket in progress; the agent gets it too

Delete project (Console) removes its board notes, its jobs with their logs and its LAW record; the code folder stays unless you tick the box, which moves it to ~/LAW/trash (deleted after the trash retention). It is refused while one of the project’s jobs runs.

Secrets

Secrets live only in ~/LAW/state/.env (mode 600) and never in git.

law secrets set LAW_TELEGRAM_TOKEN 123456:ABC...
law secrets set LAW_TELEGRAM_USER_IDS 11111111
law install                                 # starts or restarts the Telegram bot
# or: LAW Console → Settings (checks the token with Telegram first)
law secrets export ~/Desktop/law-secrets.env   # keep this in your password manager

Storage

law reclaim --dry-run   # preview
law reclaim             # remove unused model caches, old trash, temp files; prune uv/Homebrew/Docker caches
law save                # export Open WebUI presets/prompts/tools/knowledge to settings/openwebui (secret-scanned, committed, not pushed)
law restore-state       # add the saved ones that are missing on this Mac (also runs in law install)
du -sh ~/LAW/*          # where the space goes

Models are the bulk (about 200 GB). Generated files accumulate in ~/LAW/outputs/: Console → Storage → “Generated files older than a week” moves them to the trash (emptied after 7 days).

Hardware wear

Checked 2026-11-23 on the M5 Pro (1 TB SSD, 64 GB):

Part Reading What LAW does
SSD 2% of rated life used, 0 integrity errors, 100% spare; about 190 GB written per day over the last 11 days (model downloads and quantizing included) The oMLX prompt cache is capped at 20 GB; unused models and media are deleted; at this rate the SSD lasts decades
Battery 100% capacity after 48 cycles; macOS holds it at 80% on AC Leave the charge limit on while the Mac stays plugged in
Display Was kept on day and night by a keep-awake command LAW keeps the display awake only while a job runs (computer use needs it); otherwise it may sleep

Check again:

smartctl -a disk0 | grep -E "Percentage Used|Data Units Written|Media and Data"   # brew install smartmontools
system_profiler SPPowerDataType | grep -E "Cycle Count|Condition|Maximum Capacity"
ioreg -c IOBlockStorageDriver -r -w0 | grep -o '"Bytes (Write)"=[0-9]*'            # bytes written since boot

Fresh Mac or after a format

  1. Install Homebrew and Python.
  2. git clone <repo> ~/SourceCode/OpenSourceLocalAI && cd ~/SourceCode/OpenSourceLocalAI/v6
  3. ./install.sh --secrets <your exported secrets file>
  4. law doctor. The first time the operator role controls an app, approve the macOS permission prompts (System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility, Automation, Screen Recording).

Reset

law uninstall --system   # stop and remove services, containers and the ~/.zprofile block
rm -rf ~/LAW             # remove all machine-local data (models, outputs, secrets)

Troubleshooting

Docker services down after a restart: tail ~/LAW/logs/colima.log. The Colima launchd agent clears pid files that no longer belong to limactl, the cause of “vz driver is running but host agent is not”.

A project made by hand (it has .law/project.json) and missing from Console → Projects: law adopt <folder>. It shows its tickets and waits for your /go <project>. Agent tasks do this themselves when they finish.

QA fails a round that has no evidence: no test report, no checks in qa/, or, for a project with docs/design/, no design review of the screens. The designer role does that review because QA’s model cannot see images. Owner notes sent during the handover wait for the next build session, and the verify message lists them.

Symptom Check Fix
law doctor shows a service down law services logs <name> law install repairs it; or law services restart <name>
An agent step pauses for a long time with no model activity pmset -g log \| grep Sleep The Mac slept. The worker keeps it awake while jobs run (caffeinate), but closing the lid on battery still sleeps it: keep the lid open or the charger plugged in during long jobs
Jobs stay queued law jobs; worker log A heavy job may be running (one at a time by design). law services restart worker requeues safely
Very slow first answer Model is loading (about 0.25 s per GB) Normal after a swap; repeated jobs on the same model are fast
Open WebUI page empty law services logs for Colima; law install First start takes about a minute
Out of memory warnings Activity Monitor → Memory Lower context or mem_gb in the registry, or close large apps
Image pull errors during install Network inside the VM Re-run law install; it resumes and pulls one image at a time
Operator can’t control an app System Settings → Privacy & Security Allow the terminal / law under Accessibility and Automation, then retry
Open WebUI says it cannot load a model / 507 A heavy job (agent, image, video) is using the memory By design on 64 GB: only one large model fits. Pick the model already loaded, or retry when law jobs shows the job finished
Agent progress says “no file changed for 25 min: nudging” The agent was re-reading instead of building Automatic: it resumes the same session told to build and fix. Per job, stall_min in the payload changes the limit (0 turns it off)
A ticket session’s progress says “split the ticket into smaller steps” Second stall in a row in one ticket session; in a coder’s ticket only project files count as saved work, not .law/ notes Automatic: the agent splits it into <ID>.1, <ID>.2 ... (any indent); each sub-ticket gets its own session, and LAW ticks the parent when all parts are ticked
Progress says “nudging the agent to tick and commit” On a stall with uncommitted product files LAW ran .law/check.sh itself and it passed Automatic. The gate run redeploys the project’s stack when its check.sh does (Pantry’s does)
Progress says “debugging with probe files” or “edited a file with a shell command” A second probe/scratch file in one session; a heredoc, sed -i, perl -i or tee write Automatic reminders, once per session; not strikes
Progress says “OpenCode’s database is busy: retrying” OpenCode’s store under ~/LAW/data/opencode was still locked by the previous session Automatic: retries after 10, 30 and 90 s, then fails the step (Telegram offers Retry)
A pipeline ran past its planned build stages Tickets were still open when the last build stage ended (ADR-0021) By design: LAW adds a build stage, up to 64 stages in all; a stage that made no progress goes on to review instead
/proposal fails with “Mail did not respond” or “not allowed” macOS asks once whether LAW may control Mail System Settings → Privacy & Security → Automation: allow it for Mail, then resend; the PDF path is in the error
/proposal fails with “no report email set” LAW_REPORT_EMAIL missing Set it in the Console (Settings → Report email) or re-run ./install.sh
A diagram in a proposal shows as code Mermaid could not draw it The email names it; fix the block in docs/proposal/proposal.md and re-run pandoc or ask Tony to fix it
Video job very slow Expected: Wan 2.2 14B renders ~5 s of video in several minutes Use shorter clips (--seconds 3) or lower resolution in the job payload

Developing LAW itself

The installer’s venv has every dependency, so use it for checks (no separate repo venv is needed):

P=~/LAW/runtime/law-venv/bin
$P/ruff check src tests && $P/mypy src && $P/python -m pytest -q tests/unit
python3 scripts/test_report.py   # every layer, incl. live integration; writes docs/TEST-REPORT.md

After changing src/, law install --only services restarts the API, worker and Telegram bot.

The repo is public, so its hooks keep personal data out (ADR-0023). law install points git at .githooks/: pre-commit and commit-msg run gitleaks with .gitleaks.toml (default secret rules plus email, home-path, Mac-hostname and LAN-address rules), and pre-push re-checks every pushed commit and refuses any author or committer other than the GitHub noreply address. CI (.github/workflows/privacy.yml) runs the same checks over all history. Use law.paths.display() / law.privacy.scrub() for anything written into committed files. If a hook blocks you, fix the content rather than adding an allowlist entry.

Architecture

Context (C4 level 1)

flowchart LR
  user([You]) -->|Telegram| tg[Telegram cloud]
  user -->|browser / CLI / apps on the LAN| mac
  tg -->|long polling, outbound only| mac[LAW on the Mac]
  mac -->|first install only| hf[(Hugging Face, Homebrew, GHCR)]
  mac -->|web search| web[(Search engines via SearXNG)]

Containers (C4 level 2)

flowchart TB
  subgraph LAN["Your network (no login)"]
    cli[law CLI]:::client
    webui[Open WebUI :3000]
    home[Homepage :3010]
    caddy[Caddy :8000<br/>LLM front door]
    api[law API :8100]
    comfy[ComfyUI :8188]
    searx[SearXNG :8888]
  end
  subgraph Mac["Native on Metal"]
    worker[law worker<br/>model-aware scheduler]
    omlx[oMLX 127.0.0.1:8001<br/>LLM / VLM / embeddings / rerank]
    media[mflux · mlx-audio<br/>image · speech · music]
    agents[OpenCode agents]
  end
  valkey[(Valkey 127.0.0.1:6379<br/>durable queue)]
  bot[Telegram adapter] --> api
  cli --> api
  api --> valkey
  worker --> valkey
  worker --> omlx
  worker --> media
  worker --> agents
  agents --> caddy
  caddy --> omlx
  webui --> caddy
  webui --> searx
  webui --> comfy
  classDef client fill:#eef,stroke:#88a

Open WebUI, SearXNG and Homepage run in a small Colima VM (4 CPU, 4 GB). Everything that needs the GPU runs natively.

Request flow

  1. A client (Telegram, CLI, another device) posts a job to the API.
  2. The API resolves which model the job needs and how much memory, then stores it in Valkey.
  3. The worker’s scheduler picks the next job:
    • priority first (interactive > normal > batch), with ageing so nothing starves;
    • within a priority, prefer the model already loaded, then the model with the most waiting work (fewest swaps);
    • one heavy job at a time; light jobs (speech, embeddings) run alongside while memory allows.
  4. Before a heavy job the worker unloads other large models through oMLX, so a 40 GB image model never collides with a 34 GB LLM.
  5. ask jobs run as a pipeline: draft (Qwen3.8-27B) → judge (Gemma 4, a different family) → revise only if the score is below 4/5.
  6. Progress events stream back to the client; results land in ~/LAW/outputs/.

Crash safety: running jobs hold a lease. If the worker dies, its jobs return to the queue with their original age; retries back off, and jobs that keep failing go to a dead-letter set.

Memory budget (64 GB)

Slot GB
macOS and apps 12
Docker VM 4
Models (one heavy + light) 48

Non-functional requirements

Requirement How it is met Verified by
Accuracy over speed Largest quants that fit; independent judge; revise loop Integration test (judge family), eval suites
Reproducible install Registry + pinned revisions + brew bundle + uv.lock Re-run tests (0 changes), fresh-machine test
Re-runnable Each step plans from real state; lock; resumable downloads Unit tests for the six re-run guarantees
Single data root ~/LAW for everything machine-local; env vars point tools there Wipe and placement checks
No secrets in git .env only in ~/LAW/state; gitleaks Secret-scan tests
LAN access without login Services bind 0.0.0.0; oMLX stays on loopback behind Caddy Integration test on the LAN IP
Recoverable Leases, retries, dead letters, launchd KeepAlive Worker crash-recovery tests

Security posture

Decided by the user (ADR-0006): services are open to the local network without login, and agents act with the user’s full permissions. Consequences are documented in the ADR. Telegram is restricted to allow-listed user IDs because it is reachable from the internet. Valkey and oMLX bind to loopback only.

See docs/adr/ for each decision and the alternatives considered.
